title: Surface Area and Volume of 3D Objects
summary: Calculate the surface area, volume and capacity of rectangular prisms, triangular prisms and cylinders, convert between units, and describe how doubling or tripling dimensions changes surface area and volume.

notes.text: For any **right prism**, and for a cylinder (which is like a prism with a circular base), the volume is the area of the base multiplied by the height.

notes.caption: Volume of a prism or cylinder

notes.text: Unroll a cylinder and you get its **net**: two circles and a rectangle. The rectangle's length is the circumference of the circle, $2\pi r$, and its width is the height $h$.

Total surface area of a closed cylinder

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Calculate (a) its volume and (b) its total surface area. Round to two decimal places.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: If you are given the **diameter**, halve it first. A tin with diameter 8 cm has $r = 4$ cm. Also, an open container (no lid) has only **one** circle in its surface area.
Add the areas of all the faces. For a rectangular prism, $\text{SA} = 2(lb + lh + bh)$. For a triangular prism, add the two triangles and the three rectangles.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a triangular prism
notes.problem: A triangular prism has right-angled triangles with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm at its ends. It is 20 cm long. Calculate its volume and total surface area.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: The three rectangles of a prism together form one long rectangle whose length is the **perimeter of the base**. So the side area of any prism is $\text{perimeter of base} \times \text{height}$.

notes.title: Worked example 3: a water tank
notes.problem: A cylindrical water tank has radius 0,7 m and height 1,5 m. How many litres does it hold? How long does it take to fill at 20 litres per minute?

notes.text: If **all** dimensions are multiplied by $k$, surface area is multiplied by $k^2$ and volume by $k^3$. Tripling every dimension multiplies volume by $27$. If only the radius of a cylinder is doubled (height unchanged), the volume is multiplied by $4$, because $r$ is squared in $\pi r^2 h$.

items: Volume of a prism or cylinder: area of base × height. Cylinder: $V = \pi r^2 h$.
Closed cylinder: $\text{SA} = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$; the curved surface unrolls into a $2\pi r$ by $h$ rectangle.
Prisms: add all faces; side area = perimeter of base × height.

Which expression gives the area of the curved surface of a cylinder?
questions.explanation: The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle $2\pi r$ by $h$.

questions.prompt: Calculate the total surface area of a closed cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Round to two decimal places.
A cylindrical container has radius 10 cm and height 30 cm. How many litres does it hold? Round to two decimal places.
Doubling the radius of a cylinder (keeping the height the same) doubles its volume.
questions.explanation: $\pi(2r)^2h = 4\pi r^2h$: the volume is multiplied by 4.
